To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the majority of students are interested in learning about aging and (2) the majority of faculty members believe that their students need to be better prepared in aging.

(1) students in all disciplines, including those not traditionally considered to have an interest in gerontology or geriatrics, are eager to learn about the needs of older adults, and (2) interdisciplinary student aging interest group activities are a successful way to engage students in learning about older adults.

(1) the use of a theater script to teach medical students about aging is feasible, (2) it is possible to create a script that is relevant to the medical school curriculum, and (3) the script can be successfully implemented in a variety of medical schools.
